# Replication oplog window monitoring (Oplog GB/Hour, Replication Headroom) — facts

> Source-anchored units about Replication oplog window monitoring (Oplog GB/Hour, Replication Headroom): 16 across 4 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-31 · 16 units · 4 sources · rights: quote -->

## How it works

- [statement] When lag exhausts retained oplog history, a secondary can no longer catch up from that history and may require a full resync. Monitor headroom and window together to detect the approach to that boundary. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/review-available-metrics.md · keywords: Replication oplog window monitoring (Oplog GB/Hour, Replication Headroom) · also: https://docs.percona.com/percona-monitoring-and-management/3/reference/dashboards/dashboard-mongodb-replset-summary.html, https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/storage/README.md
- [statement] Atlas documentation states that replication headroom is collected at 85-second intervals regardless of project default granularity. Treat this as a sampled diagnostic signal when interpreting short workload bursts. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/review-available-metrics.md · keywords: Replication oplog window monitoring (Oplog GB/Hour, Replication Headroom)

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Ops Manager's troubleshooting documentation lists idle or infrequent writes as a possible cause of misleading reported lag and recommends checking whether lag persists; this is a documented diagnostic caveat, not evidence that every modern Atlas lag spike has that cause. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/ops-manager/current/reference/alerts/replication-lag.md · keywords: Replication oplog window monitoring (Oplog GB/Hour, Replication Headroom)

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Replication headroom is the relevant sync source oplog window minus the secondary’s replication lag; it measures remaining history margin rather than free disk space. Atlas alert documentation names the sync source, while its metric overview describes the primary. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-conditions.md · keywords: Replication oplog window monitoring (Oplog GB/Hour, Replication Headroom) · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/review-available-metrics.md
- [statement] An oplog window is workload-sensitive: rising oplog generation can shrink the window. Operational inference: compare window and lag trends after workload or capacity changes rather than treating a previous window measurement as a future guarantee. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/review-available-metrics.md · keywords: Replication oplog window monitoring (Oplog GB/Hour, Replication Headroom) · also: https://docs.percona.com/percona-monitoring-and-management/3/reference/dashboards/dashboard-mongodb-replset-summary.html

## Facts and statements

- [statement] The oplog window describes retained operation time. Percona measures the newest-to-oldest entry span in seconds; Atlas presents an estimated average in hours based on oplog churn. Normalize units before comparing either window with lag. (high confidence) — https://docs.percona.com/percona-monitoring-and-management/3/reference/dashboards/dashboard-mongodb-replset-summary.html · keywords: Replication oplog window monitoring (Oplog GB/Hour, Replication Headroom) · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/review-available-metrics.md
- [statement] Oplog GB/Hour measures the primary's average hourly generation of oplog data; a high generation rate relative to configured oplog size corresponds to a short recovery window. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/review-available-metrics.md · keywords: Replication oplog window monitoring (Oplog GB/Hour, Replication Headroom) · also: https://docs.percona.com/percona-monitoring-and-management/3/reference/dashboards/dashboard-mongodb-replset-summary.html, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-conditions.md
- [statement] Operational inference for storage auto-scaling: monitor storage separately from replication headroom. Atlas documents that insufficient oplog size can prevent disk auto-scaling; rising disk capacity therefore does not, by itself, establish adequate retained replication history. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-conditions.md · keywords: Replication oplog window monitoring (Oplog GB/Hour, Replication Headroom) · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/review-available-metrics.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/monitoring-alerts.md
- [statement] Grafana’s MongoDB integration documents separate critical alerts for excessive replication lag and low replication headroom. The public monitoring-mixins alert implementation also separates these two conditions. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://grafana.com/docs/learning-paths/mongodb-integration/install-dashboards-alerts/ · keywords: Replication oplog window monitoring (Oplog GB/Hour, Replication Headroom) · also: https://github.com/monitoring-mixins/website/blob/master/assets/mongodb/alerts.yaml
- [statement] The inspected monitoring-mixins headroom rule averages oplog spans and member optimes by job and mongodb_cluster, and fires at a non-positive result for five minutes. Inference: these averages can conceal one badly lagging secondary, so assess member-level headroom as well as aggregate alerts. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://github.com/monitoring-mixins/website/blob/master/assets/mongodb/alerts.yaml · keywords: Replication oplog window monitoring (Oplog GB/Hour, Replication Headroom) · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/review-available-metrics.md
- [statement] Atlas describes Oplog GB/Hour in terms of uncompressed oplog data. Treating this number as compressed physical disk growth would conflate different measurements. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/review-available-metrics.md · keywords: Replication oplog window monitoring (Oplog GB/Hour, Replication Headroom)
- [statement] Atlas defines Replication Headroom as the primary's replication oplog window minus the secondary's replication lag. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/review-available-metrics.md · keywords: Replication oplog window monitoring (Oplog GB/Hour, Replication Headroom)
- [statement] Monitor headroom alongside replication lag to assess whether a secondary risks falling outside retained oplog history; lag alone does not describe the remaining history margin. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/review-available-metrics.md · keywords: Replication oplog window monitoring (Oplog GB/Hour, Replication Headroom) · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/ops-manager/current/reference/alerts/replication-lag.md
- [statement] Percona's ReplSet Summary defines its recovery window as newest-entry timestamp minus oldest-entry timestamp. Its Oplog Details dashboard separately labels Oplog Range and Now to End, with the latter measured from the current time to the oldest entry; these panel definitions should not be assumed interchangeable with Atlas's churn-based estimate. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/review-available-metrics.md · keywords: Replication oplog window monitoring (Oplog GB/Hour, Replication Headroom) · also: https://docs.percona.com/percona-monitoring-and-management/3/reference/dashboards/dashboard-mongodb-replset-summary.html, https://docs.percona.com/percona-monitoring-and-management/3/reference/dashboards/dashboard-mongodb-oplog-details.html
- [statement] Percona's Oplog Details buffer-capacity panel measures fetched but unapplied entries, with Used and Max in bytes. That buffer is distinct from the time span of retained oplog history. (low confidence) — https://docs.percona.com/percona-monitoring-and-management/3/reference/dashboards/dashboard-mongodb-oplog-details.html · keywords: Replication oplog window monitoring (Oplog GB/Hour, Replication Headroom)
- [statement] Grafana Cloud's documented MongoDB integration includes a ReplicaSet dashboard and a MongodbReplicationHeadroom condition for low headroom. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://grafana.com/docs/learning-paths/mongodb-integration/install-dashboards-alerts/ · keywords: Replication oplog window monitoring (Oplog GB/Hour, Replication Headroom)
